title: Finite scalar extension of a possibly transcendental separable field
statement: Let $k\subseteq F$ and $k\subseteq E$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose $F/k$ is separable in the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], and $E/k$ is finite-dimensional. Give $U=F\otimes_k E$ its commutative tensor-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(f\otimes e)(f^{\prime}\otimes e^{\prime})=ff^{\prime}\otimes ee^{\prime}$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Then $U$ is a nonzero finite product of fields. For every prime ideal $P\subset U$, $U_P$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a field and is separable over $E$ via $e\mapsto(1\otimes e)/1$, in that same possibly transcendental sense. No separability of $E/k$ or finite generation of $F/k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, equivalence of separability and geometric reducedness; Tag 04KN, lemma-geometrically-reduced-permanence, localization; Tag 00J6, lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra, and Tag 00JA, lemma-product-local. Tensor associativity gives geometric reducedness over E before taking a field factor.

proof.text: For every extension field $H/k$, the ring $F\otimes_kH$ is reduced. Indeed, write a nilpotent $z$ as a finite sum $\sum_j f_j\otimes h_j$ and put $F_0=k(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subset F$. By the definition of separability, $F_0/k$ is separably generated. The cited separably-generated tensor lemma, applied to the reduced $k$-algebra $H$, says $F_0\otimes_kH$ is reduced. The inclusion $F_0\to F$ stays injective on tensoring with $H$, since $H$ is a flat $k$-module; commute the tensor factors to apply the cited injectivity statement. Thus the tensor $z_0$ given by the same finite sum satisfies $z_0^n=0$ whenever $z^n=0$, hence $z_0=0$ and $z=0$. This works for arbitrary $H$, without algebraicity or finite generation of $F/k$.

source.place: Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness; finite-support reduction in its first paragraph, using the existing separably generated case

proof.text: Take a finite $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $E$. The elements $1\otimes e_i$ span $U$ over $F$: expand each right tensor factor in this basis and use balancing. Consequently $U$ is finite-dimensional over $F$, so the cited finite-dimensional-algebra lemma makes it Artinian. Step 1 with $H=E$ makes it reduced. The canonical map $F\to F\otimes_kE$, $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, is injective by the cited field-extension tensor lemma. Since $F$ is nonzero, $U$ is nonzero. Neither assertion asks that $E/k$ be separable.

source.place: Tag 00J6, lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra; the finite-basis spanning calculation and nonzeroness are the scalar-extension argument

proof.text: Apply the reduced-Artinian residue-product lemma to $U$. Its set $M$ of maximal ideals is finite, each $L_m=U/m$ is a field, and $\theta:U\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{m\in M}L_m$ is the canonical $U$-algebra isomorphism. In particular it respects the given $E$-action. The set $M$ is nonempty: an empty product is the zero ring, whereas $U$ is nonzero by step 2. Each composite $E\to U\to L_m$ is a unital homomorphism between fields, hence injective, so these are genuine field extensions of $E$.

source.place: Tags 00J7 and 00JB, lemma-artinian-finite-nr-max and lemma-artinian-finite-length, reduced case; canonical quotient form of the existing residue-product lemma

proof.text: Here is the localization calculation, including every prime, using the finite product in step 3. In $V=\prod_mL_m$ let $e_m$ be the coordinate idempotents. For a prime $P$, at least one $e_m$ is outside $P$ because $\sum_me_m=1$, and at most one is outside because $e_me_n=0$ for $m\ne n$. Write $m$ for this unique index. Every element with zero $m$-coordinate is $(1-e_m)$ times itself, hence lies in $P$. No element with nonzero $m$-coordinate lies in $P$: multiplying it by the vector whose $m$-coordinate is its inverse and whose other coordinates are zero gives $e_m$. Thus $P$ is exactly the kernel of the $m$-projection. The map $V_P\to L_m$, $a/s\mapsto a_m/s_m$, is bijective: the inverse sends $b$ to the coordinate vector $b e_m/1$; the composites are identities since $e_m$ becomes $1$ after localization and all other $e_n$ become $0$. These maps preserve the $E$-action. Transporting along $\theta$ proves $U_P\cong L_m$ as $E$-algebras, in particular $U_P$ is a field.

source.place: Tag 00JA, lemma-product-local, finite-product localization calculation written explicitly from the fraction definition

proof.text: Fix $m\in M$ and an arbitrary extension $H/E$. There is an algebra isomorphism $(F\otimes_kE)\otimes_EH\cong F\otimes_kH$, sending $(f\otimes e)\otimes h$ to $f\otimes(eh)$, with inverse $f\otimes h\mapsto(f\otimes1)\otimes h$. The displayed maps respect balancing, multiplication and units and are inverse on pure tensors. The right side is reduced by step 1. The $E$-linear coordinate inclusion $L_m\to\prod_nL_n\cong U$ has the $E$-linear coordinate projection as a retraction. Tensoring these two linear maps with $H$ preserves their composite identity, so $L_m\otimes_EH\to U\otimes_EH$ is injective. This inclusion preserves multiplication, although it need not preserve the unit; that suffices: a nilpotent maps to a nilpotent and is therefore zero by injectivity. Hence $L_m\otimes_EH$ is reduced for every $H/E$.

source.place: Tag 04KN, lemma-geometrically-reduced-permanence, geometric reducedness of a field factor; here proved directly using its split coordinate inclusion and the explicit tensor reassociation

proof.text: If $E$ has characteristic zero, apply the characteristic-zero separability lemma to $L_m/E$. Otherwise the characteristic of the field $E$ is a prime $p>0$; apply the geometrically-reduced-extension separability lemma with base field $E$, extension $L_m$, and the reducedness for every $H/E$ just established in step 5. In either case $L_m/E$ is separable in the possibly transcendental sense. Step 4 identifies $U_P$ with such an $L_m$ over $E$. A field isomorphism over $E$ takes finitely generated intermediate fields to finitely generated intermediate fields and takes a separating transcendence basis and its separable minimal polynomials to their images; thus this notion of separability is invariant under that isomorphism. The structural map is the stipulated $e\mapsto(1\otimes e)/1$, since the localization comparison in step 4 respects $E$.

Step 1: a nilpotent has finitely many tensor terms, so it already lies in F_0⊗H with F_0 a finitely generated subfield; F_0 is separably generated by def (2), so F_0⊗H is reduced, and flatness makes F_0⊗H→F⊗H injective, so the nilpotent is zero. Step 2: U is finite-dimensional over F, hence Artinian; it is reduced by step 1 with H=E and nonzero because F→F⊗E is injective. Step 3: the reduced-Artinian residue product gives a finite product of fields; the empty case is excluded by step 2, and E→L_m is injective. Step 4: elementary check that every prime is the kernel of exactly one coordinate projection, and that U_P≅L_m over E; I verified both composites. Step 5: (F⊗_kE)⊗_EH≅F⊗_kH, and the E-linear coordinate inclusion has a retraction, so it stays injective after ⊗_E H; it is multiplicative but not unital, which is enough to show L_m⊗_EH is reduced for every H/E. Step 6: characteristic 0 uses the char-zero lemma; characteristic p uses the 030W node with base E. Stacks 030W (algebra.tex l.10360) does assume char p>0, so the case split is needed and correct. Separability is transported along the E-isomorphism of step 4. Edge cases checked: E=k; F=k with E purely inseparable; k=F_p(s), F=k(t), E=k(s^{1/p}), where U=E(t); E/k split by F into several factors. No duplicate states the item: I checked spec-finite-product-fields, finite-georeduced-etale, finite-galois tensor decomposition and trf-geometrically-reduced-base-change. Step 4 could cite spec-finite-product-fields (1) but writes the argument out in full; not a fault. It is generic flatness, not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality or of their proofs, and it is already cited widely outside sec-trace-formula, so I accept it. I also accept the declared tool_use of the 030W geometric-reducedness criterion: it proves a field-algebra subclaim and does not replace a route step. No fixes.
